component: POP parser state and line length

quotes.text:
/* Provide a common means of detecting empty lines in a message. i.e. to detect the end of headers among other things...*/
#define EMPTY_MESSAGE_LINE(buf) (buf[0] == '\r' || buf[0] == '\n' || buf[0] == '\0')

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: EMPTY_MESSAGE_LINE accepts CR, LF or a zero byte. In ParseFolderLine, an empty signal finalizes headers only while the parser is in ParseHeadersState, then switches to ParseBodyState even after a parse error to stop accumulating headers. An empty signal with length zero does not add input bytes to m_position. It is a parser completion signal, not a stored extra blank line or a replacement for the POP line-reader protocol. Reuse the existing From-body/envelope guard lesson instead of combining those distinct boundaries. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build or accessibility session was run. Full bug and review discussion remains pending.
title: Keep the POP empty-header signal within parser state semantics
